brief: Higher oil and higher rates dragged stocks down until a Reuters headline reporting a US-Iran phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz snapped indices back to unchanged; an Iranian source denied the report within an hour, and oil rebounded on the denial. Brent rose above $100 amid Saudi interception of Houthi missiles and an Iranian escalation threat, while Dated Brent's backwardation and the WTI cash roll signaled physical tightness. Rates rose further on hawkish Fed commentary (Barr, Paulson, Hammack, Williams), weak 5Y/7Y auctions and a smaller-than-expected Treasury buyback, pushing the 10Y to 5.18% intraday; market pricing (70% October, 80% December hike odds) now sits more hawkish than the Fed's own dots, and bond vol exceeded equity vol for the first time in a year. Stocks closed roughly unchanged as the Iran-deal rumor offset the selloff, even as AI credit anxiety grew: Oracle's CDS hit a record high after it declared force majeure on its Project Jupiter data center, adding to hyperscaler credit stress despite modest hyperscaler equity gains. The dollar extended gains, pulling gold below $4,300; bitcoin held near $84,000.
